caveats: macro_f1 is engine-vs-oracle agreement on a hand-labeled quality canary (10 events, 4 scored rules), not field detection fidelity; see docs/detection-quality.md.
per-rule confusion counts are graded per corpus FILE, not per event.

per-rule expected-positives are corpus-composition-dependent (this row read corpus commits {'evtx': '4ceed2f4706daf601c212a8f91c113dd85349a2c', 'splunk': 'eac2f8f675ec31a6618003399dcc53641524e673'}; a newer upstream corpus is a pin bump in a PR): on this snapshot's run password_spray had zero expected-positive files in every corpus (reported as untested); eval/attack/fire_check.py separately proves every MITRE-tagged rule fires on its own real producer fixture.

password_spray: graded on committed synthetic fixtures (eval/detection_accuracy/attack_fixtures.py), published only in fixture_per_rule_confusion -- never in per_rule_confusion, corpus_records or parser_coverage_pct.

parser_coverage_pct is a corpus-shape measurement: it means 'that share of THIS EVTX corpus's Security+Sysmon records parse', not 'that share of all log formats FENGARDE can ingest'; most of the 19 shipped parsers cover IT/OT formats these corpora do not contain.
twin metrics are harness-measured on a deterministic in-process plc simulator replay (seed 7, basis=harness-measured); null fields were not measured in that run, not zero.
ci-clone contamination: GitHub clone counts are inflated by authenticated Actions checkouts and are NOT published here as traction evidence.

units.alert_reduction_ratio: dimensionless [0,1]; 1 - (WS-8 incidents / raw WS-4 alerts) over the scenario window
units.attribution_accuracy: dimensionless [0,1]; share of ACTOR-BEARING scenario steps whose attributed actor matches ground truth (actor-less steps excluded, not credited)
units.chain_fidelity: dimensionless [0,1]; share of the oracle's ALLOWED causal step-pairs that a real WS-8 incident-graph edge joined
units.corpus_commits: git commit of each corpus the lanes read ({evtx, splunk}), pinned in eval/detection_accuracy/fetch_corpora.sh; null on older rows
units.corpus_files: files each corpus lane read ({evtx, splunk}); null on rows written before provenance was recorded
units.evidence_completeness: dimensionless [0,1]; share of the oracle's per-step evidence fields present on parsed steps (unparsed gap steps count against it)
units.false_correlation_rate: dimensionless [0,1], LOWER IS BETTER; share of the oracle's FORBIDDEN causal step-pairs (allowed: false) that a real WS-8 graph edge joined anyway -- 1.0 means every forbidden pair was falsely joined
units.fixture_per_rule_confusion: counts of committed synthetic fixtures (tp/fp/fn/tn) per rule, graded exactly like a corpus file, counted once; null when the row predates separate grading
units.fixture_tested_rules: rule names with expected-positives from synthetic fixtures (when also listed in untested_rules: ONLY from fixtures)
units.fpr: dimensionless [0,1]; share of the twin's benign negative-control replays that raised an incident
units.incident_reconstruction_time_ms: milliseconds, informational wall-clock: median time to assemble the real WS-3 evidence package for the picked incident; machine-load dependent
units.macro_f1: dimensionless, [0,1]; unweighted mean of per-rule F1 (engine-vs-oracle agreement on the hand-labeled detection-quality canary, tools/detection_quality_eval.py) -- NOT field detection fidelity
units.mttd_seconds: seconds from chain start to the first chain step whose oracle-expected rule fired, on seed-derived event timestamps of ONE deterministic scenario (not a mean over incidents, not wall-clock)
units.mtti_seconds: MODELED, not measured: the real investigation step count over the picked incident's own graph x a documented 30 s/step analyst-latency constant (eval/twin/report.py _ANALYST_STEP_SECONDS); null when no incident promoted
units.mttr_seconds: null by construction: the twin has no remediation/closure event to time (not measured, not zero)
units.parser_coverage_pct: percent; share of Security+Sysmon records in the EVTX corpus (records_supported / (records_security + records_sysmon)) that a shipped parser can normalize at all -- corpus-shape-limited, see methodology.md
units.per_rule_confusion: counts of corpus FILES (tp/fp/fn/tn) per rule, NOT events: each third-party corpus file with supported records is replayed through the real WS-2->WS-4 pipeline and graded against an independent oracle; synthetic fixtures excluded
units.severity_calibration_error: binary 0/1, NOT a mean error: 0.0 when the peak fired alert score lies inside the oracle's severity band, 1.0 when outside; null when nothing fired
units.tpr: dimensionless [0,1]; share of the scenario's oracle-expected detections that fired on the twin's intrusion-chain replay
units.untested_rules: rule names with zero expected-positive corpus files (tp+fn == 0) in the latest corpus run -- surfaced, never implied passing
